entries.title: Introduction to Zechariah
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
ZEchariah is the second Prophet who cometh from God to the returned Captives, and his errand to them was both to second Haggai's Exhortations, and to reveal more fully, then he doth, all the future Revolutions and Events to the final desolation of Jerusalem, and the second Temple by the Romans, and the rejection of the Jews for their sins against all the Mercies of their God, and for their rejecting and murthering of the Messiah, who, rejected of the Jews, ta[illegible]eth in the Gentiles, and establisheth his Church amongst them, which is revealed unto Zechariah, and Communicated to the Jews by him, with a Declaration of the future ruine of the Persian Kingdom by the Graecians, and also of the Wars of the Seleucidae, and Lagidae, and their overthrow by the Romans, during the series of which times, the Jews shall be grown Numerous, Wealthy, and Powerful, and so long as they keep their Covenant with God, shall do wonderful things, and be eminently owned of God, and be either wonderfully secured amidst these t[illegible]oubles, or more wonderfully victorious over those that trouble them. And indeed what Zechariah foretold, or promised to them, was in its time made good amongst them, his predictions were punctually fulfilled, if the promises were not, it was because the Jews by their sins cut themselves off f[illegible]om the promises, which may be observed in those intervails of times between Zechariah's Prophecying, and the coming of the Messiah; now the first intervail was above Two Hundred years to the Death of Alexander Magnus, during which time, the Jews enjoyed the common peace with the Subjects of the Persian Empire, and the particular favour of Alexander the Conquerour, during his Life. These years were years of growth to the Jews: The next intervail through the Wars of Alexander's divided C[illegible]ptains, and between the Selcucidae and the Lagidae was an intervail of some great troubles, and yet of greater preservation to the Jews. The next intervail is that of the Maccabees, during which, those Victories were g[illegible]tten, which do almost exceed our belief, but whilest thus times were changed, the Jews continued much the same, unthankful to God, cold in Religion, and added to their sins dayly, till at last God delivered them into the hands of the Romans, whose General, Pompeius Magnus deposed Hyrcanus from the Th[illegible]one, and restored the High Priesthood to him, from henceforth the Jews Sins and Miseries grow together till that Zech 14.2. was accomplisht, the City Jerusalem taken, the Houses rifled, &c. thus by various intermixture of Providences, God did try the Jews whether they would, as became his People, repent of former sins, amend their future doings believe his promises, and obey his precepts, that he might bless them; so should al[illegible] the good (foretold by this Prophet) have crown'd them. But if th[illegible]y fail'd, (as they did) in those points of Duty, then a[illegible]l the evil threatned should (as it did) overtake them, and as Zechar[illegible]ah foretold, continue on them as it doth [illegible]o this day. This Prophesie then contains th[illegible] Revolutions of the Jews, and the Empires of Persia and Greece, and the Romans; in whose times the Jews by killing the Lord of Life, filled up their measure, and by whose hands God punisht them, destroying their polity, rasing their City, burning their Temple, and captivating the People, which lasteth to this day, the better to represent all these at once to your view, take this following Scheme.

Zechariah doth either

  • 1. Exhort to present Repentance and Reformation, chap. 1, 2, and chap. 7, 8.
  • 2. Promise
    • Present Blessings, chap. 1, 2. and chap. 8, 9, to 15.
    • Future Mercy, and that
      • under Persian Government, c 8.3, 4, 5, 6, 7.
      • Alexander and the Graecians, chap. 9.8.
      • In the Maccabees times.
        • chap. 9.12, 13, 14, 15. chap. 12.6.
  • 3. Encourage
    • Joshua chap. 3.
    • Zerubbabel chap. 4.
  • 4. Threatens the
    • Enemies of the Jews.
      • chap. 1.21. chap. 2.9.
      • chap. 9. from 1. to 8.
      • chap. 12.1, 2, 3, 4, and 9.
    • sinful and impenitent Jews, ch. 4. ch. 11.1. ch. 14.1, 2.
  • 5. Foretel the
    • Messiah's coming
      • chap. 3.8, 9, 10. c. 6. c. 8.19, 20, 21. and chap. 9.9, 10. chap. 13.7.
    • Jews rejecting him, chap. 11.10, 11, 12, &c.
    • Gods
      • Avenging this sin on the Jews, chap. 14.1, 2.
      • Calling in the Gentiles, c. 8.20, 21, 22, 23. c. 12.10. and c. 3.8, 9. and c. 6.12, 13, &c.
      • Continued Protection of the Church of Christ among the Gentiles, chap. 14. from ver. 3. to the end.

All which either in dark, yet significant Types or Emblems is represented to us by this Prophet, or else in plain, and easily intelligible words.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Called both Maris[illegible]uan, and Bul, by Hebr. and answers to part of our October and November. Two Moneths after Haggai began to encourage the Iews to build the Temple.

Ezra 4.24.

b Son of Hystaspes, and the third Persian Monarch. vid. Hag. 1. ver. 1. let. a. and again chap. 1. ver. 15. let. f. at large.

c Here is his Warrant, and Divine Call, the Lord communicated to him what he was to communicate to others.

Ez. 5.1.

d His Name bespeaks him a remembrancer of God, or it may speak God remembring him, and the rest of this people.

The Iews call'd the Descendents in right line Sons, though they were Grand-Sons, or great Grand-Sons; and in this sense s[illegible]me say Zechariah is the Son of Baruch, and the Son of Iddo. This Zechariah is not he that is mentioned 2 Chron. 24.20. this is too early by many years, nor is this Zechariah the Father of Iohn Baptist, this is a[illegible] much too late, but most likely 'tis that Zechariah whom the Iews slew between the Temple and the Altar, Matth. 23.35.

e This Name is expresly mentioned Mat. 23. and his time exactly suits the time, pointed at by the Evangelist.

f One of this name you have 2 Chron. 9.29. but this is too old to be this in the Text, [illegible]or there will be found (as Wolphius in Ezram notes) 450 years distance between Iddo the Seer, and this Iddo mentioned in the Text.

g Whether Zechariah, or Iddo, I determine not.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f The Holy, the Mighty one, your God, the just Governour of the World.

Heb. with [illegible]spans[illegible].

g So long provoked, that his displeasure at last enkindled within his Breast, and broke out into that flame which hath consumed your Land, City, and Temple.

h All that were Progenitors, [illegible]ore-Fathers to the return'd Captives, from their entrance into Canaan, but specially since the Apostacy in Ierob[illegible]am's time, for many hundred years your Predecessours have provoked God by their notorious sins, even to the days of their Captivity.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i And, Heb.

k Command, and Require.

l Of the Captivity who are returned to their own land.

m In my Name, by the Authority I have over them as Lord of Hosts, require they hear, and obey.

Jer. 25.5. [illegible] 35.14. [illegible]. 7.19. [illegible]. 3.7.

n Repent ye of all your sins, leave them, set your hearts on my Law to obey it, on my Worship to give me it, on my Temple to reedifie it.

o Who can punish your refusal, who can protect you in your return, and reward your Obedience

p with blessings, with all blessings, which my presence brings to a repenting people. It was woe with you, and your Fathers, when I departed from them, but it shall be as well with them, when I return unto them.

q That you may be assured hereof, I promise it to you, and will be engaged to perform, as Lord of hosts, as having all things at my disposal.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r You who have seen the sorrows of a long Captivity, who are wonderfully brought back, who are under the teachings of Rod and Staff.

s All the former Prophets, 2 Chron. 36.15, 16.

t Preached earnestly, frequently, and compassionately.

Jer. 18.11.

u Now to day, yet before 'tis too late: O! turn from vitious, sinful courses and wayes; from your Atheism, Idolatry, Murthers, Oppressions, and Adulteries.

x It is repeated that it might be more impressive upon them. The Prophets importunately intreated them to cease from evil, Isa. 1.16. and 31.6. Ier. 3.12. Ezek. 18.30. and Hos. 14.1.

y They did not, because they would not, they regarded not what I said by my Prophets, neither could they be perswaded to it.

z This obstinate disobedience is twice together charged on them, to make their sin appear in its greatness.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a But where are your disobedient Fathers? Are they not buried in a strange Land? Did they not die of those Diseases? Were they not consumed with Famine, and the Sword, as was menaced against them?

b Some apply this to the false Prophets who promised peace, but where are they now? But 'tis better understood of the true Prophets, who died as others; they do not, nor must live always to warn you.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f The dreadful Menaces which I spake by my Prophets.

g The d[illegible]creed Judgments which my provoked Justice resolved to execute on them,

h which by my Prophets as my Heraulds I proclaimed, and published.

Or, overtake.

i Overtake as a pursuing Enemy overtakes, and se[illegible]eth on his Enemy, and spoileth him; have not my Judgments thus taken hold both on your Fathers, and on you?

k By this it should seem that Zechariah gave them time to consider what answer to give.

[illegible]am. 1.18.

l It is true as God said he would do, so he hath done against us, our Fathers, our Families, our Ci[illegible]ies and Temples. God's words have not failed they dyed not, though our Fathers did: This may be an abstract of their Repentance.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m Which answers to part of our Ianuary.

n Vid. Hag 1.1. let. a. b. and ver. 15. let. f.

o See ver. 1. let. c.

p Vid. ver. 1. let. d. e. f. g. The first Sermon Zechariah preacht, was three Moneths before this, and that Sermon was reproof, which probably had good effect, as ver. 6. let. k. l.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q In a Vision God communicates his Word, Mind, or Will to the Prophet.

r Either litera[illegible]ly, it was by night that Zechariah had this Vision, or with this it may note the obscurity and misteriousness of the Vi[illegible]on, for it may be emblematical, as the Myrtles, and the bottom are.

s Mark well what I saw, as now I relate it to you.

Josh. 5.13.

t One in a humane shape, Christ Jesus in shape of a Man, so he appeared to Ezek. 1.26. and 40.3. and to Daniel, chap. 7.13.

u In a posture of readiness, speed and resolution to help his people, and to appear for them in some tokens of greatness and majesty, Psal. 45.4.

x Both the Beast is noted, Horse, bold, strong, speedy, and gallant; and the colour is noted also in the same colour he appeared to Isaiah, chap. 63. ver. 1, 2, 3. and Revel. 6.4. This colour is a symbol of his coming to avenge his own just quarrel, and the uniust dealings of his, and his peoples Enemies.

y he posteth himself in a convenient place to observe and be ready, (as needful) among humble, verdant, fragrant, pleasant, and much valued Trees, emblem of the flourishing, fruitful, and excell[illegible]nt Saints, and Servants of God.

z This bottom or low Valley in which the Myr[illegible]les grew, (proba[illegible]ly on some Rivers bank) is an emblem of the Church in a low, mourning, afflicted State, then 'tis most verdant, and fragrant [illegible] these Trees; or as Spices bruised in a Mortar.

a Christ was [illegible] beseems a Captain, in the head, the rest as his Souldiers or Sevan[illegible]s are behind attending on him.

chap 6.1. to 7.

b Horses of the same colour, not without their riders, though they are not exprest, but 'tis a Synechdoche, Horses, and Horse-men are both intended, and these are Angel[illegible], ver. 10. now the colour of these Horses is 1. Red, denoting probably the bloody condition of States and K[illegible]ngdoms by Wars one against another, either when God punisheth his Church, or when he avengeth himself, and his Church on his Enemies, and hers, which will appear on a survey of the times past, when Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Gr[illegible]cia[illegible] or Roman Empires, did successively by Wars do Gods w[illegible]rk, his strange work, &c. Isa. chap. 10. and chap. 14.

Or, bay.

c A mixt colour, made up partly of white, red and black, as some guess, an Emblem of Affairs of different complexion, not all prosperous, nor all unprosperous; not all dark, nor all light, as the day the Prophet describes neither day nor night, such times did the Iews know, during the 70 Prophetick weeks, from the beginning of them, to the Messiah's coming.

d An Emblem of the best dayes and State the Church should be in, so Revel. 19.11.14. and the Empire too with it.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
e So soon as he had seen and observed,

f Zechariah,

g This was Christ the Lord of Hosts.

h What is the me[illegible]n[illegible]ng of these Appearances or Visions?

i Christ, the Angel of the Covenant, so I take this Angel that promiseth to inform the Prophet to be the same that appears as a Man on the Red Horse among the Myrtles.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k Vid. ver. 8. let. t. u. x. y.

l Gave answer to what I asked.

m Horsemen.

n A periphrasis of Angels, who are Servants, and Ministers of the Divine Providence in the Government of the World.

o God is pleas'd a[illegible]ter the manner of men to speak of his managing the affairs of the World; men must employ others, because they need them, God will employ Angels, though he needs them not.

p The Empires which his Churches were either help'd or injur'd by; These were partly by the Pride of their Emperours, partly by the flattery of their Servants and Ministers, and partly by the Ignorance of the World at that time in matters of Geography thought to be the whole Earth; and the Scripture sometimes useth phrases, used and well known among men, though there be some impropriety in them.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q The ministerial Angels, signified by the horses and horsemen.

r Or rather the Angel, the Lord, the uncreated Angel, who sent them out, and receives account what they had done.

t As men who would give an exact account, survey every part, so we have search'd all Nations, and Kingdoms; walk'd the length and breadth of them.

u The World, but chiefly through the Babylonish Empire, which accounts it self Lord of all the Earth.

x 'Tis wonderful to be seen, and therefore we beseech thee, O Lord, to behold, and consider this.

y As having ended their Toil, or weather'd the storm, composed their differences, and shea[illegible]h'd their Swords, are full of peace, and sit still to take their case.

z Either the same thing repeated, to heighten the quiet of these states, or to confirm the Truth of the thing, or to express the inward quiet of mind the people had with their outward quiet. The publick peaceable, and every ones mind satisfied, this is the state of the Earth, the Empire which at that time ruled all.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a When the surveying Angels had made their report of the Prosperity of the Heathen.

b The Angel, the Lord Christ, Mediator of the Church, and head of the Church.

c Prays as one interceding.

d Christ speaks to his Father, speaks as one much affected with the state of his afflicted Church.

e It is the expostulation that well befits a praying Soul, it is not the enquiry of a discontented mind, but the request of one longing for mercy. So David, Psal. 13.1, 2. and the souls under the Altar, Rev. 6.10.

Ierusalem, thy chosen Mountain, heir of Promises to be re-edified, and on Iudah's Cities too, of whose rebuilding, peace and pr[illegible]sperity thou hast, O Lord, spoken great things, Ier. 30.31.32. and 33. Chapters, and Ezek. 36. and 37, &c. chapters.

f They have felt thine anger and hot displeasure, it was just, and is so still; but it is not to be perpetual; thine anger hath smoaked against the sheep of thy Pasture.

Dan. 9.2.

g The term prefixt for the captivity is fully come, 'tis the seventieth year of thei[illegible] miserable captivity; now shew mercy, build Sion, and glorifie thy self in doing it, for the set time is come. It is now 70 years since thy Temple was burnt, and Ierusalem sack'd. And full 80 years since Ieconias with many of thy people were carried captive into Babylon, and somewhat more, since many were carried with Iehoiachim, from which to the second of Darius are much about eighty eight, or nine years.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h God the Father.

i Christ, the uncreated Angel, Lord of Angels and Redeemer of Israel.

k Who had first talked by signs and Visions, and next by explaining the mind, and meaning of them, and answering the enquiries Zechariah made.

l Suitable, and seasonable.

m The words minister'd comfort to Ierusalem and the Captives, the words imported deliverance and blessings.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n i. e. When the Father had heard the Son and answered him; this is spoken to our apprehension, and so must be understood.

o Of the Covenant, the Lord Christ.

p Vid. ver. 13. let. k.

q Now publish what thou hearest, preach by commission from me, and assure my poor, captive, impoverish'd Church, that God, my God and her God, will do good for her.

r Publish what God, Lord of hosts, and Father of his People, promised to do for them.

chap. 8.2.

s I have been jealous against, but now am jealous for Ierusalem; my love is now heightened to a very high degree of compassion for my People, and of Indignation against her Enemies and Oppressors.

t The City called by my name.

u Where my Temple stood; those Gates of Zion, which I loved more than all the dwellings of Iacob.

x That Zeal I bear, and now will shew for them is great, to a wonder; it is the Zeal of a God who infinitely loves and pitieth his people.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:15
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y The Lord of hosts, God of Israel.

z Exceedingly angry and will shew it that they may see and feel it, my displeasure is grown up to the highest against them.

a Secure in their strength, sing a requiem to themselves and trouble to Israel. See ver. 11. let. y. z,

Isa. 47.6.

b With mine own people, i. e. in comparison with the anger I bear against the heathen, 'twas little, Psal. 137. tot.

c The Heathen, Babylonians.

d Attempted to destroy whom I would but correct, Isa. 10. & 14. I whipt to smart, you wounded to blood, I did wound to bind up, you did wound to kill, &c. It is an Anthropopath[illegible]ia.

e It was more than they could do to provoke me more against them than their own sins did; but what I permitted for a while, they did, and added to the Affliction of Israel. I would prune, but they struck at the root.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:16
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Because the Enemy hath so barbarously and inhumanely added affliction to the afflicted, 'tis time to save and relieve.

g When I was departed, and had withdrawn my Presence, thus cruelly were my people handled; but now I will return, I will be with them, my presence shall restrain the violent, and protect the innocent.

h With tender, abundant, and promised Mercies now they shall be comforted indeed.

i The Temple of God, the Excellency of Iacob.

k Shall be finish'd, the impediments shall be removed, what glory I have promised by Haggai, chap. 2.9. I will put upon this house of mine in Ierusalem.

l This confirms the promise, and establisheth our Faith, if we know the import hereof.

m The builders measuring line shall be stretch'd out, to mark out Walls, Gates, Palaces, Streets, and Houses in Ierusalem, that they may be built again in beauty, and strength, with skill, and art; and shall be once more the glory of the Earth, and Joy of Israel.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:17
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n The Prophets Commission is either enlarged, or more full instructions given to him, to raise the hope and stablish the Faith of the People of God.

o Jerusalem, and the Cities of Judah are mine, saith the Lord, and as mine I'le build, beautifie, enrich, fortifie, defend, and enlarge them.

Heb. [illegible]

p Through increase of Families and Persons, they shall send forth Colonies, and plant new Towns and Cities, and through increase of Wealth, and Cattel be able to build their cities, and stock their Colonies.

q Swarm as Bees, and send out their young ones.

r Their God.

s Zion his Church, with comforts fit for a Church.

Isa. 1[illegible].[illegible]. chap. 2.11.

t Type of the civil State as here joyn'd with Zion; the Kingdom shall be blest in it self, and be a blessing to others, much like that Hos. 14.4, 5. all this an effect of my choosing it, and dwelling in it.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:18
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u After I had seen those things, and heard those comfortable words, and received commission to publish all the good news I had heard.

x He was so intent before, that he look'd on nothing else; now he lifts up his eyes.

y Clearly, certainly, and distinctly.

z Emblems of the Enemies of the Jewes, for strength, fierceness, and pride, and for their number, from all parts of the World.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:19
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a The Prophet prays for Information from the Angel, from Christ, who is the best Teacher.

b What may be the meaning of these horns, which I see, and know to be horns, and four in number.

c Powers, States and Kingdoms, which have from all sides push'd at, broken and tossed my people, sorely bruised some, and destroy'd others, these Horns are probably on the North, the Syrians, Assyrians, and Babylonians; on the East, the Moabites and Ammonites; on the South, Edomites and Egyptians; on the West the Philistines. All which had many a time spoiled the Jewes.

d The Two Tribes which were the Kingdom of Judah.

e The Ten Tribes carried away by Salmaniser, or the Reliques of Israel, which adhered to the house of David.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:20
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Jehovah, who before is the Angel, i. e. Christ, he is the Eternal one, the great God.

g Both proposed the thing to be seen, and gave eyes to see, and discern it.

h Known by their Garb and Tools to be Carpenters or Smiths, as the Hebrew bears it.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:21
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i So soon as I could propose the question, immediately upon sight of the Carpenters.

k Zechariah.

l He saw they were men, enquires not who they were, but what was their business, and design; perhaps 'tis fittest for us to rest also in the knowledge of what they are to do, and enquire no farther who they were.

m The Lord Christ inform'd the Prophet.

n Christ doth in order to satisfie the enquiry first point to the four horns of which ver. 18, 19, as if he should have said look you there are four horns which have done mischief to Judah.

o Kept them so under, none had either strength or courage to lift up the head, and thus these horns proudly and cruelly destroy'd my People.

p These Carpenters or Smiths are Emblems of those Instruments God will employ in breaking these destroyers. Here are four carpenters to break the four Horns.

q To strike a fear into them first; these Kingdoms signified by horns, shall lose their courage.

r Then their Authority, and power shall be cast out easily.

s Heathen round about Judea.

t Have employ'd their Arms and strength against.

u The whole Kingdom of Judah, Gods people.

x To drive them out of Gods inheritance. See ver. 19. let. d.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Zechariah.

b This is the third Emblem, or Vision he had seen.

c Very diligently, and intently.

d One in form of a man, some say 'twas Christ, others say a Type of Nehemiah, it was an Emblem of some Master-builder to be sure, and its probable the Prophet took him for no more than a man.

e He appear'd ready and prepar'd to lay out the platform of Jerusalem for extent, form, and beauty.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f It is evident, the Prophet did not in so bold a manner enquire before, which may possibly be for that he apprehended this man to be one lesser than an Angel; nor doth he ask the meaning of this Hieroglyphick, but understanding what it meant, the Prophet enquires onely where the platform was to be laid.

S[illegible]e Rev. 11.1.

g To take the exact dimensions of it, that it may answer Gods Promise, and be capable to receive its inhabitants.

h The city which was to be built hereafter, but first the Temple is to be built.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i The great and glorious Angel, i. e· Christ Jesus himself, which had so long talked with Zechariah.

k From the midst of the Myrtle-trees, where he was first seen; whither he is going is not said, perhaps to stand by, direct, and encourage, the person that was going to measure Jerusalem.

l A created Angel, or a Ministerial Angel, as became his office, offers his service to Christ.

m Who is Lord of Angels.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n Or, And he said. Or as the French, (lequel lui dit) which said unto him, so 'tis plain, that the Angel which now was going [illegible]orth, spake to that Angel which came to meet him, or gave him orders what to do.

o Since you come so seasonably, hasten with all diligence and from me tell that young man, Zechariah.

p Which hath so long lain in rubbish, which I once delighted in, which now seems desolate, and hopeless.

q Filled with inhabitants.

r The Suburbs of it shall be as Towns unwalled for greatness of extent, and for safety, and freedom, from enemies and danger; Their own multitudes of men shall be some safeguard to them. And they shall have my presence, a better safeguard.

s Brought thither for sacred uses, for sacrifices.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
t What was promis'd or foretold in the former Verse is ratified in this by an account how it should be performed.

u That a thing so much above the hope of a present dejected people, so much too great for so weak, and so few a people, might be believed and expected, God engageth he will perform the word.

x Which cannot be scaled, it would consume them that attempt it; nor undermined, none could come so near it. Such a wall as once was Elisha's Guard, 2 King. 6.16, 17. verses; to which this place may possibly refer. Or 'tis allusion to the manner of Shepherds and Travellers in those Countreys full of wild beasts to make fires in the night to secure themselves.

y No part shall be unguarded, or open to the Enemy.

Isa. 60.19.

z My Presence, and favour shall make her glorious, Isa. 4.5, 6.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Since Ierusalem shall be safe, rich and glorious by the presence and blessings of her God, the Prophet calls to the sleepy Jewes, as men that need be awakned.

b Set upon your Journey for your own countrey and city, come out from your captive Prisons.

Is[illegible]. 48.20. & [illegible].11. Jer. [illegible]. and 51. [illegible]word Rev. 18.4.

c Make all the haste you possibly can, and flee as men do who are pursued with danger, as men that are earnestly bent to get out of harms way, as the man-slayer to the city of Refuge. Heb. hath onely And flee, but our Translators have by that guested at what might fill up the expression, and read, Come forth, &c.

d Babylon which lay North to Canaan.

e As I executed my threats in scattering you, so I will perform my promise, and gather you from all quarters of the World; arise, come away therefore.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f The Proclamation for free return is publish'd, up then and be gone.

g O ye people who should dwell in Sion, ye daughters of Sion.

h Keepest in Babylon when thou mightest go to Jerusalem.

i Perhaps this intimates that which kept many Jews in Babylon, Wives or Mistresses.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k Some refer this to what went before, as a reason why the Jewes should return, for God hath commanded it. I think 'tis an encouragement to the Jewes to return, because God had promised to make them a glory, and now assures them that he will take a very particular care of them, therefore sends his Son, as a Judge, or Vindex, against the Nations that had spoiled the Jewes, or God sends his Son to them to inform them that 'tis their interest to unite with the Jewes, and become the people of God, and be partakers of the Glory, and safety of Gods Israel. However to let them understand that 'twill be dangerous to do violence to Israel, as it would be dangerous to any one to violate what is most dear to him that can destroy the offender; to tell them Israel is the Apple of Gods Eye.

Deut. 32.10. Psal. 17.8.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
l Or lift up.

m My power and strength.

n Against the Nation and Kingdom that doth violence to the people, who are my glory, and I am theirs, saith the Lord.

o Those people who comply not with him whom God sendeth.

p Shall be overthrown and spoiled, and become a prey.

q The Jewes who were first spoiled by, and then made servants to the Nations who conquer'd, captivated and hardly used the Jewes, and indeed this fulfill'd in Esthers days, and in the Maccabees times.

chap. 4.9.

r Either Jewes, or Heathen, or both.

s Be convinced and own it.

t The great and faithful God.

u Hath commissioned Christ to inform them who are to make their choice what to do herein.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Isa. 12.6. & 54.1. Zeph. 3.14.

x Now Christ calls them to Rejoice in the goodness shewed to them, and to sing forth the Praises of him who shewed it.

y The whole Nation of the Jewes, the peculiar, redeemed and restored people of God. They that had been in great and long captivity.

z To execute Judgments on thine Adversaries, to complete thy deliverance and salvation, I come as foretold and promised, in the dispensations of Providence among the Nations, in the performance of Promises to you my people.

Lev. 26.12. Ezek. 37.27. Joh. 1.14. 2 Cor. 6.16.

a Pitch my Tabernacle, nay, build my Habitation, and House, and reside in it, give you my Ordinances, my Blessing, and my Presence. This was fulfill'd in part presently, and so through near 500 years, till Christ came, and ever since to his Gospel Church.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
b And great Heb. implieth both multitudes, and greatness of Nations; or Heathen, and Gentiles; as the word beareth.

c Become proselytes, enquire for, adhere to, and worship the God of Israel.

d When God shall lift up his hand for his people against their Enemies, as Esther 8.17. when Christ shall be come in the Flesh, and shall take down the partition wall.

e Covenant-people, to love fear, worship, and obey Christ.

f See ver. 10. let. a.

g See ver. 9. let. s.

h The Sovereign Law-giver, and Almighty Ruler of Heaven and Earth.

i The Messiah, and Zechariah his Servant.

k Jew and Gentile.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
l Jehovah, the God of Abraham, and of his seed, who had cast off Judah, and seem'd to quit his claim in his antient inheritance, by a disseism of 70 years.

m Claim, recover, possess and delight, as a man doth in his paternal inheritance,

n All his Israel, this Tribe mentioned, but all the rest included.

o His Treasure and peculiar people; his lot and part.

p Upon, Heb. holy, not by any inherent holiness, but holy and selected, and set apart for a holy people consecrated to God.

chap. 1.17.

q The Lord will as of old choose Ierusalem for his seat.

entries.title: Zechariah 2:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Zeph. 1.7.

r Murmur not, you that love not Zion; dispute not, you that think these promises are too good, too great; but in silence, Reverence, and adore God in all his Excellencies and wayes; wait, and expect the accomplishment of all, by him who never utters more than he can and will do for his People.

s Both Iew and Gentile; you are weak, short fighted, and worthless; you are flesh, be silent and wait.

t The Wise, Mighty, Gracious, and Faithful one; who never suffer'd a word of his to fall unfulfill'd, nor will let any of these promises to fail.

u He speaks to our capacity, God is said to be raised in allusion to men who get up, or rise up, and set about what they will do; so here God is on this work already.

Heb. the habitation of his Holiness. Deut. 26.15.

x Either Heaven, or his Temple.

entries.title: Zechariah 3:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a The Lord of hosts, whose Servant Zechariah was, and in whose name he spake.

b In vision represented to me Zechariah.

Hag. 1.[illegible].

c For that office was by hereditary right descended on him, and how mean so ever his state was, yet still he was that great Officer of the Church,

d Either as accused, and to make his defence; or rather Ministring in his office, according to his Duty.

e This Angel was Christ, whose Minister, or Servant the High Priest was, as well as Type of him.

That is, an adversary.

g Either because the accusation was true, or to hold his working hand from its work.

Heb. be his adversary.

h Ioshua.

s That Adversary, as we might render the word, either Satan the Devil, or some instrument of his stirr'd up by him, Sanballat, or &c.

entries.title: Zechariah 3:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
l i. e. Christ the great Redeemer, Restorer, Lord and Mediator of the Church.

Jude 9.

m The Great God Father of our Lord Jesus Christ who as Mediator rather chooseth to rebuke him in his Fathers Name, then in his own; though this he could have done.

o He who was accused, was Gods High Priest, and to minister in the Temple at Ierusalem the City which God had chosen, in which respect it was sure that God would take cognisance of the Matter and Judge aright. He would prohibit Satan's attempts.

p This man, this Ioshua.

q Like a brand half burnt, or all smutty with long lying in the fire of Affliction? Reject him not for this

entries.title: Zechariah 3:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r At the time Zechariah saw this Vision he saw also in what a mean dirty, and totter'd garb he was, who represented the High Priest.

s It was the Hieroglyphick of Ioshua, not Ioshua himself.

t Emblem of a poor or sinful state, or both.

u Vid. ver. 1. let. d.

x The Lord Christ called, The Angel.

entries.title: Zechariah 3:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y The Lord Christ who purifieth his Church, who purgeth away her sin, and clothes her with rich and clean garments.

z So the Heb. and so this Prophet speaks, though no question went before. It is an Idiom of that Language.

a Commanded.

b Some of the attendants, those Ministerial Angels, who were Christs Servants, and as such are represented standing before him.

c Remove, or cause them to be removed, from him as altogether unbeseeming his Person, Office and employment; These filthy Garments those Angels took away, but another hand takes away what is signified by this Emblem.

d From this High-priest Ioshua.

Christ the Lamb of God.

e What Angels could not take away, Christ did, he removed the filth of Sin, the guilt and stain of it.

f Adorn and beautifie.

g O Ioshua.

h Clean and Rich, Emblem of Graces, and spiritual Excellencies given to him.

entries.title: Zechariah 3:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i Zechariah takes the boldness to desire that for Ioshua, which might adde to his Veneration, and Authority, and he asks the thing of Christ, or rather Christ commandeth this be done.

k Who Minister before Christ.

chap. [illegible]

l A rich and beautiful ornament for the head of the High Priest, not a Crown, which is for Royal heads, but a Tire, a Pontifical Ensign.

m As they were commanded by Christ at the request of the Prophet.

n All the Garments which did appertain to the High Priest, of which you read Exod. 28.4. which probably were put on though they are not expresly mention'd here.

o The Angel who is the Lord Christ himself.

p Withdrew not till all this was done.

entries.title: Zechariah 3:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q The Lord Christ.

r Solemnly declared, and averr'd it, gave him to know.

entries.title: Zechariah 3:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s The Father whose will Christ reveals to us.

t Io[illegible]hua.

u Obey the Precepts and holy commands of the Law.

Or, [illegible]

x The special charge, and office of the High Priest.

y Be chief, and Ruler in the Temple, and in the things that pertain to the worship of God there.

z Not as a door-keeper or Servant, but as the Chief, on whom others may wait, and give attendance, and at last shalt have place among glorious Angels, Heb. 12.22

He[illegible] [illegible]

entries.title: Zechariah 3:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Hitherto thou hast been entertained with Emblems and Hieroglyphicks, but now O Ioshua, hear what these mean

b The other Priests, thy Associates in the Priestly Office, tho' inferiour to thee.

c As Assessors or Coadjutors in a Council, or Assembly, the High Priest as President, the other as Members of the Council sate with him, to let them know what these Types mean.

Ps[illegible] [illegible] Isa. [illegible].1[illegible]

Heb. [illegible]

d The worldly, prophane, unbelieving and ignorant sort of Iewes wonder at them, and their hopes; at their labour and expences in attempting to build such a house, with so little helps to raise such a Structure out of Rubbish.

e God the Father

f will bring forth a much more wonderful work.

Isa. 42.1[illegible] 52.13

Jer. [illegible] chap. 6.[illegible] Luk. 1.[illegible]

g Christ Messiah, the Branch, Isa. 4.2. and 11.1. Ier. 33.15.

entries.title: Zechariah 3:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h Here is an Ellipsis, and to make it up we must repeat that of the 8th. ve[illegible]se, Hear now, &c. For behold, (pointing to a particular stone) that stone which I have laid, saith God, in the sight of Ioshua, or which he saw laid in the building of the Temple.

[illegible] Isa. 2[illegible].[illegible]

i On that one stone are seven eyes, and Ioshua and his fellows are commanded to observe it, the meaning of which the Angel will suggest to them presently, it is not improbable this one stone might be a corner stone, and a principal corner stone, and the Eyes Engraven on it, so placed, that they might look many wayes; so 'twill be a more exact Emblem of Christ the chief corner stone, and of his perfect knowledge and wisdom, fitting him to govern his Church, and provide for it.

chap. [illegible] Rev. 5.[illegible].

k The Engraving Engraved, i. e. most artificially, lively, and with excellent contrivance.

l Or, and I have removed, I have pardoned the iniquity of this Land at once. Thus the Emblem or Type, which I shall once more set before you in plainer words, then those of our Version. Hear now, O Ioshua, thou and thy fellowes, for behold there is one stone, and on that stone seven eyes, most curiously Engraved, and this laid in thy sight, and in the sight of thy fellowes; This learn by it, that the Temple, founded on such a corner stone, built by the wisdom of the chief Builder, guarded and watcht over by all-seeing Providence, is the blessing and honour of that people, whose sins are all forgiven. The farther spiritual meaning discovers the Messiah, the chief corner stone, the Gospel Church founded thereon, guided by perfect Wisdom, and preserved by never erring Providence, and blest with the pardon of all her sins, taken away in one day, by the Meritorious death of her Redeemer.

entries.title: Zechariah 3:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m Of Building my Temple, when 'tis finisht, and in the day of removing the sins of my people, literally referring to the returned captive Iewes, Mystically, to the whole Church in Gospel dayes, when Christ the chief corner stone, shall have purged away sin, and establisht his Church.

n Invite with love and peace, such as becomes Neighbours, who are partakers of the same Grace of God, and Blessings of a Redeemer.

[illegible] 4.4.

o To feast or refresh themselves under the pleasing shadow, and with the sweet delicious fruit of the Vine and Fig-tree, of both which there were ever greatest store, and of choicest taste, when the people of God; the Iewes did obey, worship and fear the Lord, and long for the Messiah, and loved each other.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Christ, who for some time had left Zechariah, and bestow'd some time on new dressing and cleansing, and adorning Ioshua, the High Priest.

b This is the fourth time of Christs revealing his mind to this Prophet by Vision.

c Either roused him out of a drousie fit, and bodily sleep, or out of an extasie, or wonder, that surprising him, he was as if asleep, or shaked him out of a sluggish negligence, or an observance of these things.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
d What dost thou discern, of that thou didst before half asleep, half awake see, but didst not observe.

e Since awakened and rowzed; I have very diligently viewed, and observed, and I see.

f By Gods appointment there was a candlestick to be made, as a Utensil and Ornament of the Temple, Exod. 25.31.

g So was the candlestick to be for the Temple, all of pure Gold, Exod. 37.17,

i On the highest part of the candlestick, on the top of the candlestick on the top of the shaft, or on the head of the candlestick.

l One pipe to each Lamp, the mouth of which pipe joined to the Bowl or Basin, and received oyl from it; the other end of the pipe fastned to the lamp convey'd oyl into the Lamp.

m So each of the seven Lamps had a pipe reaching from it to the Bowl or Basin.

n These Lamps were so set as to stand somewhat higher than the Body of the candlestick.

b Or Basin, or round, and large oyl cruet, capable of so much oyl, as would suffice to feed all the Lamps in the Candlestick.

k Either so many, because the Temple candlestick had just so many, or because of some perfection supposed to be in this Septenary Number.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o Some say Branches; better Trees, which well rooted, will continue, and perpetually supply the Bowls, and that will supply the Lamps.

p Not more, or fewer than two.

q So placed that the candlestick stood between them, and each Tree stood at distance from the candlestick, on the right, and left hand thereof; that they might distil their oil into the Basin or Bowl. All which is an Emblem of the Church, both what it is made of, pure Gold; what made for, to be light in the World; to shine as Lamps that continually burn, maintain'd with pure oil, distilled from the Olive Trees, not pressed out by man but continually, freely, and abundantly dropping or flowing from these olive Trees.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r After that I had seen and discerned.

s See chap. 3. ver. 4. let. z.

u See chap. 1. ver. 9. let. h.

t See chap. 1. ver. 19. let. a. and chap. 2. ver. 3. let. i.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
x When the Prophet had enquired into the meaning of these emblems.

y See chap. 1.19. let. a.

z 'Tis not a question either to upbraid the Prophet as an Ignoramus, Christ doth not reproach his for not knowing deep, and dark mysteries at first sight of them. Nor is it the question of one that was uncertain about the thing enquired into, Christ knew the Prophets ignorance though he ask the question, but 'tis to excite him to attend and learn.

a Zechariah freely confesseth he knew not, he pretends not to know what indeed he did not know.

b He owns the greatness and sovereignty of Christ.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c So soon as Zechariah had owned his Nescience.

d Christ.

e Or this word of the Lord is to Zerubbabel, 'tis particularly designed to him, and in an Emblem prefigureth what a Church, how precious as Gold, how full of light, how framed, how maintained it should be by God himself. This Hieroglyphick is a representation of what the Church should be.

f The Governour, on whose hand much of the care and trouble of building the Temple did lie; yet let him not be discouraged, for this work lyeth on God.

Or, army.

g Or by an Army, as the word bears, Heb. you may think you shall need an Army to defend you in carrying on this Building, which ill will of Neighbours about you hindereth, but I tell you there is no need of an Army.

h Courage and Valour, all which make Armes considerable, no need of this neither. Or might and power here may be of the same impor[illegible] and added only for elegancy and assurance of the thing.

i Which garnished the Heavens and can beautifie the Church, which moved upon the darkness in the Creation, and brought forth a beautiful and mighty structure, and can do as much now; by spirit we may understand either the Third Person of the Trinity engaged in Building the Church, with the Father and the Son; or by Spirit you may understand the power of God. Either is encouragement enough, and secureth the future effect, and promiseth a future State of the Church, pure and precious as Gold, full of knowledge in the Doctrines of God, as this Candlestick with seven Lamps full of Holiness from abundant measures of Grace, persevering in it by continued supplies from the Spirit of Grace in Ordinances, &c.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k The Angel having resolved the question about building the Temple, either himself doth deride all the power of opposers, or the Prophet doth triumph over it who art thou? Sanballat and Confederates, or Satan, or Babylon, or all put together what are you all? compar'd with the power of God the Lord of Hosts who by his Spirit will finish this work?

l Thou standest in the way of my Servant, and thinkest his weakness, and poverty cannot remove thee, but if he cannot surmount thy height I will bring it down and make thee as a plain, and my servant shall as easily go on with my work as a Traveller goeth over a way plain'd before him.

Zerubbabel as the Servant of Christ.

m Shall, as is usual, assist at the laying of the last finishing stone, as well as he saw and assisted when the first foundation stone was laid

n of the second Temple.

Ezra 3.11, 13.

o With loud acclamations the signs of great joy, and satisfaction in the thing done.

p Praying, and wishing all prosperity, and a long continuance of it, to the Temple and those that are to Worship God in it, as Grace and favour of God began, and finisht, so may the same grace ever dwell in it, and replenish it.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: q Either at another time, or else at the same time was added what now Zechariah declares.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r Perhaps (as is customary) he did lay the first stone with his own hands, or rather his direction, and command, and under his conduct.

Ezra 3.10.

s In the second year of Cyrus perhaps fourty years agone, likelier seventeen, but be those years more or less, he shall finish it, thus the Prophet expresly promiseth from the Lord, both continuance of Zerubbabels Life, Care and Power, as also his success in this work to encourage both him, and the Jews.

and 6.15.

chap. 2.9, 1[illegible]. and 6.15.

t Whoever thou art, that dost hear me, both Zerubbabel and all among the Jews

u Shall be fully assured, and certainly know

x God of Truth and Mercy, our God from our Fathers who remembers his Covenant,

y commanded me to preach these things.

z Returned Captives, and poor builders of this stately and magnificent house.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a And now for those that despised small beginnings, who they are is well known, and to them I say, and promise what they expected not.

b Of which Haggai 2.3.

Or, sith the seven eyes of the LORD shall rejoice.

c Or but, not withstanding they so much undervalued the meanness of the second Temple, yet when finisht they shall with many others rejoice in it.

Heb. stone of tin.

d The perp[illegible]ndi[illegible]ular with which Zer[illegible]babel shall try the finished work, or the work near finishing.

e In subordination to, and co-w[illegible]rking wi[illegible]h the Divine Providence exprest emblematically by the seven [illegible] w[illegible]re on that stone, of which chap. 3.[illegible]. Though [illegible] were prudent in managing all the affairs of Jews, Ierusa[illegible]em, and the Temple, yet not his prudence, but infinite wisdom of God gave success, and when the success app[illegible]ars in the finishing of the Temple then shall it be acknowledged an admi[illegible]able work of the Divine Wisdom, and the Jews shall conf[illegible]s th[illegible] the eyes of the Lord which run to, and fro through the whole [illegible] have been upon them in this work for good, and that God hath shew'd himself on their behalf.

2 Chron. 16.9. Prov. 15.3.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: In the eleventh verse the Prophet proposeth a question to which no answer is given, but he doth immediately proceed to ask one more question, though somewhat, yet not much different from the former, and in the answer to this latter question the Prophet acquies[illegible]eth. The explication of the 11th. verse you have ver. 3. of this chapter.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f I went on to discourse, which is the signification of the Heb. phrase here used.

g Heb. a second time

h The Angel that talked with the Prophet.

i Two principal branches one in each Tree, fuller of berries, higher then the rest and hanging over the golden pipes.

Heb. by the hand.

k These were fastened to the golden bowl, on each side one with a hole through the sides of the bowl, to let the oyl tha[illegible] distil'd into them from those Olive-branches, [illegible]un into the [illegible]owl, and out of that bowl it was through so many golden pipes conv[illegible]d into the seven L[illegible]mps

Or, empty out of themselves oyl into the gold.

l Fre[illegible]ly without any viol[illegible]e offered, drop the oyl out of themselves, yet so that still they are [illegible]ull of oyl f[illegible]r perpetual supply to the Lamps.

Heb. the gold.

m Because of its [illegible] or from its colour.

n A supernatural work and emblem of supernatural grace, these branches filled from the True Olive-tree, ever empty themselves and are ever full, so are the Gospel Ordinances filled by Christ, alwayes filling his members true Christians, and even full for all Believers.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: Vid. ver. 5. let. z. a. b.

entries.title: Zechariah 4:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Rev. 11.4.

Heb. sons of oyl.

o Not Enoch and Elias, nor the two witnesses, nor Peter and Paul, nor the two Churches of Jew and Gentile. Nor principally Zerubbabel and Ioshua, though perhaps the exposition may gla[illegible]ce upon them, and the two Orders Magistracy and Mininistry, in them; as these are Types of Christ in his two Offices, King and Priest, or Christ and the Comforter, in this I determine nothing.

chap. 6.5.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Or, And, Hebr. i. e. after I had seen those comfortable visions, and been instructed in the true meaning of them.

b Changed his posture, though the occasion of it be not mentioned, nor the posture into which he put himself.

c Look't up into the Air where the Vision appeared

d very diligently, and discerned clearly.

e A Volume, or book which in those days were not written as now our Books are printed and bound, but were written as deeds are now on large or long Parchments, and rowled up upon a neat round stick, or else rowled up on themselves, such the roll here seen, much as our large Geographical Maps are rolled upon rollers, and lodged in a convenient Cavity, so were their books of old. But probably here now the Roll was spread out at large, flying in the Air swiftly, perhaps with some noise that might make the Prophet look about him.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f The Angel, chap. 4. ver. 1, 5.

g O Z[illegible]hariah,

h That is ten yards long by this it appears the roll was spread out, for had it been rolled up, he could not have seen the length, tho' he did the breadth, five yards.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i The Angel which instructed the Prophet.

k This Roll or Book containeth the Curse, the menaced Punishment due to sinners, of which too many were still among the Iews.

l That goeth speedily, for it flyeth.

m Either the whole Land of Iudea, or over all the world, where ever these sins are found; this curse will come upon the sinners, unless they repen[illegible].

Or, [illegible] doth.

n Theft is here first mentioned, a sin that had abounded among them, and from which they were not free then, they rob'd one another, and they rob'd God, they were sacrilegious.

o Shall be punished with an extermination of his house, as well as with cutting off his Life.

p According to the just threats of the Law

r Profanely, or [illegible]alsly, the perjur'd person shall be cut off too.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s So exemplarily will I execute this Judgment, that it shall appear I do it, my hand [illegible]aith God shall be seen in it.

t None shall be able to keep it out, this curse shall come with commission from me,

u where he laid up that he got by the[illegible]t and thought to rejoice i[illegible] it, or by house understand all his Estate and Goods with his Family and posterity.

x The Robbers of God, and of their Neighbours and every other notorious transgressour of the precepts of the second Table.

chap. [illegible]

y This doth explain that of the third verse, and 'tis plain that the perjur'd person is here threatned, every one that dares call God to witness to a falsehood, and imprecate themselves if they spea[illegible] not truth.

z This curse shall be a long curse, it shall stick close to them and theirs like Gehazi's Leprosie.

a As in the heart and center of their house like a sword in the midst of the Bowels, or like a Disease that seizeth the heart.

See [illegible] 45

b Though it do not destroy suddenly, it shall destroy surely.

c The strength of it, nothing shall remain as when both Timber and stones of a house are consumed and wasted. Such execution shall be done on those whose name and place shall be blotted out.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
d Or went on, proceeded, or as we read it went forth from some more retired place, though he do not tell us what it was, or where he was with the Prophet when the last Vision appeared.

e Now the Prophet was come forth with the Angel, he is commanded to look up and observe what he seeth going forth from Ierusalem, or the Temple.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Zechariah knew not what this was he saw, so far was he from knowing what it meant.

g The Angel,

i Out of the Temple of Ierusalem.

k Having told the Prophet what the thing was, the Angel addeth once and above.

l This how dark soever it may seem to be, is a clear Emblem of this people every where. Thus there is a limited time and measure for them whilest they sin and are filling up the Ephah with their sins, they will find that the Ephah of Wrath filled up also to be poured out upon them, or as the Hebr. Thi[illegible] their eye as the Gallick Version. This the eye I have upon them, &c. i. e. God's eye observes how they fill their Ephah with sin, that he may sutably punish, that his Ephah of Wrath may f[illegible]ll also.

h the greatest, say some, of measures with the Hebrews, but their Corus was much greater, it was a great measure, and many times taken for any measure, when strictly taken, it held some three bushels.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m Here is another part of this Vision,

n Either lifted up from out of the Ephah, or brought thither to cover it.

Or, [illegible]

o A large piece of Lead of a Talent weight, large as the mouth of the Ephah.

p A Woman, the third in the Vision or Emblem.

q Secure, shameless, and resolved of her way in increasing in [illegible]in.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r The Angel unfolds the Riddle.

s This Woman that sits in the Ephah represents the sinful Nation of the Iews, is Emblem of their wickedness.

t In the abstract, to express the greatness of the Iews wickedness, they will grow up to be most wicked.

u The Angel cast down this Woman wickedness from the seat she sat on, ver.

x And now she is down the weight of Lead which she can never lift up, or remove is laid upon the mouth of the Ephah, she is shut up, as in a Prison to [illegible]u[illegible]er the punishment of all her sins. This is their res[illegible]mblance.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y Vid. ver. 1. let. c.

z ibid let. d.

a From the same place whence the Ephah came.

b The sinful Nation was resembled to a Woman, and now to keep a decorum in the Vision. They who are to be God's Executioners, to punish that wicked Woman, are called Women; 'tis like enough to be meant of the Romans, a warlike and stout Nation.

c They are set forth as having wings, like the wings of Storks, large and strong, and as flying before the wind with great swiftness, so should Divine Vengeance swiftly follow, and certainly overtake the Iewi[illegible]h Nation when after their return out of Captivity they shall corrupt themselves, and fill up the measure of their sins.

d The Judgments came thus flying, and so bare away with them those that are to be punished: It is a secret intimation of a future deportation, or carrying the Iews into captivity again for sin.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
e When I saw the Ephah, Woman imprisoned, and lead too on the wings of those two Women in motion.

f Zechariah.

g To what place, and how far.

h Not as a Nurse carryeth the Child, but as Criminals are carryed to punishment.

entries.title: Zechariah 5:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
[illegible]. 2[illegible].5 23.

i Not in Mercy, but in Judgment as intending the next deportation should not be as the first for seventy years, but for ever, they should never return

k Of Babylon whither many of the Iews fled, and so by voluntary exile fulfilled this prophesie, whither others of them were forced by the Romans.

l There they shall be confined without hope of release,

m not on the foundation of God's Promise and Covenant, but the base of their sins.

The Angel gives him an answer fuller than his question, and first tells the Prophet what was to be done with it.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a See chap. 5. ver. 1. let. b.

b Ibid let. c. d.

c The appearance or Emblem is plain enough, we can easily conceive that; but the things signified hereby are most difficultly found out, and perhaps not found when we think they are; here then, if any were, all are bound to write modestly, and all are bound to read carefully, and to judge candidly; whether by these Chariots are meant. 1. The various changes made by Wars in the Nations, the Chariots as some say were Chariots for War, and drawn by several coloured Horses, and thus Wars and Mutations thereby might be signified. 2. Or, the four Monarchies of different temper and carriage toward the Iews and others, whom they ruled as very many Learned Expositors think Or, 3. The four Gospels, with the Apostles and Preachers of the Gospel sent by Christ as others. Or, 4. Angels who are sometimes stiled Chariots of God, and who are by the Prophets, Daniel, Ezekiel, Zechariah, and by the Apocalypses introduced as great Ministers and Servants of Christ in the Affairs of his Church, I determine not, though perhaps all these might fairly be woven into one web, in which Angels as employed in the Affairs of Church and Empire, act their part in the revolution and changes of things, be these of what temper soever they will in both, till the Gospel be preached by the M[illegible]iah, and his Apostles.

d Out of a deep, shady, and dark Valley which here is laid between two Mountains so God's Judgments are a great deep, whilest his Righteousness is as the great Mountains, Psal. 36.6.

e These Mountains appear to the Prophet very wonderful, for they were of Brass to denote the immoveable decrees of God, his steddy executions of his Councels, the insuperable restraints upon all Empires and Councels which God keeps within the Barriers of such impregnable Mountains, whence not one can start till he open the way, and possibly it may import the pressures, difficulties, and distresses of the times signified hereby.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f may signifie bloody times, a fiery execution of wrath, Rev. 6.4.

g A time of Mortality, and wasting Diseases, Rev. 6.5.

There is no distinction made between Chariot and Chariot, nor any mention made of the drivers of these Chariots, though these are included in the Chariots. Now by the different colours of the Horses doth the Prophet distinguish the Chariots, and possibly that is all intended by the various colours, though generally Interpreters do guess by the colour of the Horses what should be the quality and temper of the times pointed at; of which a little,

entries.title: Zechariah 6:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h Joyful and prosperous Affairs, see chap. 1. ver. 8. let. d.

i State of Affairs mixt of good and bad, chap. 1.8. let. c.

Or, strong.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: Vide chap. 5. ver. 5. and chap. 1. ver. 19.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k Signifie or are the emblems of

Or, winds.

l Winds, Heb. to which the Empires are compared, Dan. 7.2. and for the bustlings of them may be well compared so, and forasmuch as they are raised by the Lord, and are under his command may properly enough be called winds of Heavens, which blow as God orders. Or, Spirits of, i. e. Angels of Heaven, who have as Ministers of the Divine Providence, a great share in the manage of affairs both of Church and States. Or, the impulses of Gods Spirit moving as he pleaseth in the Kingdoms of men, and in his Church. Indeed this is the great spring which moves Angels and sets them on work about what is to be done by them, either for or against States and Kingdoms, especially in reference to the Church of God.

m Which as they Refide in heaven, till employ'd, so go thence when imploy'd, and observe the will of their God in Heaven and having done their work return thither again.

1 King. 22.19. chap. 4.14, Luk. 1.19.

n They stand as Servants attending the Will and Command of their Lord.

o Their· God is Lord of all and their business to do his Will in all the Earth, not in one onely part, but every where, whithersoever they are sent.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
p The Angel signified by the black Horses, the Executioners of God's just displeasure against sinners.

q In [illegible]he second Chariot, for nothing is said more of the first, (the red Horses) say some, because that bloody and cruel State was expired, but the sad things portended by the black Horse are to come next on the Scene.

r Babylon, the whole Kingdom of Babylon, which lay so much North from Iudea, and because the Metropolis lay North, the whole Kingdom is called the North Countrey, which must feel the effects of these black Horses, which was executed by the hands of the Medes and Persians assisted by that Squadron of Angels which appeared in the second place.

s Ministers of Goodness, Mercy, and Kindness went after the black, and their business was, say some, to dispose Affairs for the benefit and joy of God's people in Babylon, whether these were sent to preserve them, to conduct them, and bring them back, and here was great work in this, for many staid behind till Ezra, and Nehemiah's time,

u The Angels signified by these, and whose business as some guess, lay in managing the Roman power, which was a mixture of many different people, and which were sometimes favourable, sometimes fierce and severe to those they had to do with.

x Egypt and Arabia, which lay South of Iudea, and which the Romans did, though late, subdue, it may perhaps point at their invading Africa too, whose punishments were mixed somewhat with Kindness and Mercy more than the Punishments of Babylon were.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y From the place where the Prophet saw them at first standing as at the starting place,

z Either asked Commission, or waited for it,

a They had a larger Commission say some the whole Earth or a particular Commission to keep their rounds in the Land of Iudea, and to take care of their affairs for the comfort of that people.

b Christ who hath all power in Heaven and on Earth,

c Stay no longer here hasten to your charge, as you have desired, so do.

d They obey immediately and do his Commands. These Bay horses are here represented as attempting, or making essay which at first seems to take little effect though at last by a full Commission empowred they do succeed in the attempt. This might give ground to suppose here is some Kingdom aimed at, which made some attempts to enlarge it self through all the Earth but failed in its attempt, which no wonder since the Angels which were to assist were not Commissioned to walk through the whole Earth, and they keeping to their commission gave no farther help for want of whi[illegible]h the design failed. How far this may concern Goths and Vandals, or any more late Empires and Kingdoms, I have neither skill nor will farther to enquire. Nor yet to enquire whether these Bay horses were not emblems of Angels employed by the Lord, in the Government of the rest of the Kingdoms of the World remote from Iudaea, but not remote from Gods Wise and Sovereign Providence governing all the Earth. The known Empires here are supposed to have been managed by particular Angels represented according to the analogy between the colours of the Horses and the complexion of the Kingdoms. And it may seem likely that the rest of the World was not le[illegible]t without some to have care of them.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
e When the Prophet had been informed about the former vision.

f The Angel that talked with the Prophet, i. e. The Lord Christ spake aloud, and called to him.

g Or are gone, for he speaks of what was already past, 'tis likely he meaneth the Red horses.

h Into Babylon.

i Either by doing what I appointed them against the cruel Chaldeans in revenge of my peoples injuries, or bringing my people back out of Babylon into Canaan.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k It appears not that this next thing hath any necessary connexion to that which the Prophet last saw.

l The direction or command for the Prophet to do something out of hand.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m Gold and Silver, of those that are come out of Babylon lately, to make their Oblation to the Lord, or to bring the Oblation of them, who yet were in Babylon, but remembred Ierusalem and the Temple.

n Go fetch them if they lodge elsewhere, and bring them in thy company.

o The same day in which they come, or else in the same day that I speak unto thee, delay not.

p Some say he was a Goldsmith, others, that he was Treasurer for the Temple, and that these persons before named had brought a rich present to him for the Temple, and the service of the Lord.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q This reiterating the command, both confirms and explains the former command.

chap. 3.5.

r Two, the one of Silver, the other of Gold.

s Put both of them, i. e. one after the other.

t Who now in this circumstance stands a Type of Christ, King and Priest for ever for his people, and this extraordinary Act was to represent something extraordinary in the Messiah.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u Ioshua but in hearing of others, and in the name of the Lord·

x Consider throughly the import and meaning of this unusual Ceremony.

y Thou Ioshua art the Type or Figure, but he that is the man signified by thee, is that great person God hath promised, and you do expect, and who shall come.

z Whom you know by the name of the Branch, who was called so long since, Messiah Ben David; This wonderful person is the man that is crowned, as King and Priest by Proxy, or in Effigy: Thou O Ioshua art the Pourtrait he is the Branch it self, chap. 3.8.

Or, branch up [illegible]rom und[illegible]r him.

a Though you may perhaps suspect the Root dry or dead, yet assuredly 'tis not, the Branch will spring up, Messiah King and Priest shall be born in due time.

b Of the same Tribe and Family, and in the same place, foretold.

c He it is, though uns[illegible]en, that stands by you, that build the Material Temple: N[illegible]ther Zerubbabel nor Ioshua, nor all the Iewes, could do any thing without Christ in the present building, which is yet far inferiour to the Spiritual Temple, which Christ will build, beautifie and preserve, and dwell in for ever.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
d The promise is repeated to settle the Iewes in the assured expectation of the thing.

e Your Material Temple as Type, and the Spiritual Temple as Antitype.

f Of both Kingly Office, and Priestly, the glory of both those Crowns shall abide on him, the only person worthy of i[illegible].

g Which speaks both his Royal Magnificence, and the Perpetuity of it.

h Though he shall have many Attendants and Offic[illegible]rs, yet he shall Rule, give Lawes, distribute Rewards and punish Of[illegible]enders,

i His by Birth, by Donation, by Purchase, and by Conquest, his most undoubtedly by best Right.

[illegible] He[illegible]. 3

k The great High Priest, to offer the great Sacrifice to God, to make reconciliation, to intercede for his People; This is that meant by the crowns set on thy head, O Ioshua.

l The peace made for Gods People shall rest upon these two, the Kingly and Priestly Office of Christ, by his Priestly Office he shall make their peace with God, by his Kingly Office he shall deliver them from Spiritual enemies; by Priestly Operation he shall expiate our sin, by the power of his Kingly Office he shall extirpate sin; as Priest he makes, as King maintains Peace; Purchase as a Priest, Protect as a King.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m Those two crowns before mentioned, made of the Gold and Silver brought from Babylon, verse 11.

n These Persons we know no more of with any certainty, but their names.

o Of their incredulity say some, of their liberality say others, but these crowns were certainly to be memorials of the Mess[illegible]ahs certain and speedy coming, and to be reserved in the Temple, as a Memorial of this solemn Typical inauguration of Io[illegible]h[illegible], or Messiah in him.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:15
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
p Such Jews as do now abide in Baby[illegible] and Persia, or other remote parts. 'Tis also the character of the Gentiles, Acts 2.42. Eph. 2.13, 14.

q The Jews did so with their gifts, came to Ierusalem and built with their brethren, the Gentiles are come in and build the spiritual Temple.

chap [illegible]

r The accomplishment of this shall prove my words to be Gods word, and that I am sent of him.

s The literal part shall come to pass in your day, if you will obey the voice of the Lord your God speaking by me. The mystical part shall come to passe also, and, if you will believe and obey, the Gentiles shall come in and be your Brethren, make up one Church with you, and help to build the Temple, the spiritual Temple. But if you obey not you shall be cast out and the Gentiles be taken in to be Gods people, and to build his Temple.

This verse hath certainly a double reference one to the Jews, and the building of the material Temple, which is the literal and historical sense, the other mystical, and refers to the bringing in of the Gentiles.

entries.title: Zechariah 7:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a A most usual form of speech introductory to what shall afterwards be spoken,

b When the Jews had now been two years in building the Temple, and probably 'twas in good forwardness.

c Son of Hystaspis about An. Mundi 3487. as Arch-Bishop Vsher in his Annals.

d Part of our November and December, when half the time of building the Temple was spent.

entries.title: Zechariah 7:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
e Either the Captives which still continued in Babylon, or the Jews returned out of captivity, but dwelt in the Countrey at distance from Ierusalem.

f Temple, which now half built began to be frequented by Priests and People, and where Haggai and Zecharia[illegible] might be found true Prophets.

g It appears not who these were, but no doubt they were eminent in dignity and piety.

h Train either of Friends that accompanied them. Or, of Servants that waited on them.

[illegible]

i In most solem[illegible] manner, and with Sacrifices no doubt, for the Altar was set up long ago. Now these come to intreat the face of the Lord by Prayer in the house of Prayer for pardon of what was past, and acceptance of them at present, and for answer to their enquiry.

entries.title: Zechariah 7:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k To consult with.

l They were to be the ordinary casuists, and ought to be able, and ready to answer all cases of Conscience, as Mal. 2.7.

m Had their residence in, or about the Temple.

n These were extraordinary casuists, who might be supposed able to satisfie the enquiry, if the Priests could not. These Prophets were Haggai and Zechariah.

o i. e. Fast, of which weeping was a part, 1 Sam[illegible]el chapter 1. verse 7. and Matth. 9.15.

p In sad remembrance of the burning of the Temple on the 10th. day of that month.

q From worldly cares and designs, and afflicting my self.

r This intimateth their former practice, and seems to include in it some little boasting of it.

s It had been easie for them to have reckoned up the exact number of years, but they choose rather to express it thus, to greaten their performance.

entries.title: Zechariah 7:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
t When these men had proposed their case, and expected the Priests answer.
